-85.58920,42.98790.name: Michigan Reproductive & IVF Center, PC
-85.58920,42.98790.desc: A fertility clinic reporting to the CDC's National ART Surveillance System. Medical director: Valerie I. Shavell, MD. A fertility clinic is where human embryos are made, selected and stored, and where assisted reproduction happens, like IVF, ICSI, egg and sperm donation, freezing embryos and eggs for later. Reporting is required of every US clinic performing assisted reproduction, under the Fertility Clinic Success Rate and Certification Act, so this is close to a complete register rather than a list of members. What it records is cycles started, which is not the same as children born.

2.33791,48.84150.desc: A clinic mapped in OpenStreetMap as offering fertility treatment. 5.43971,52.52273.name: Wageningen Bioveterinary Research
5.43971,52.52273.desc: An organisation accredited by AAALAC International for its care and use of laboratory animals. Part of Wageningen University & Research. Accreditation is voluntary and paid for, so this is a list of organisations that chose to be inspected rather than a register of everyone doing the work. An organisation absent from it is not accredited; that says nothing about whether it uses animals. In several countries the largest users are absent for exactly that reason. The directory gives a city and country and no street address, so this point marks where the organisation is registered rather than the building where animals are held.

-73.55678,45.51163.name: Centre de recherche du Centre hospitalier de l’Université de Montréal
-73.55678,45.51163.status: Certificate of GAP Last visit: interim, April 2025
-73.55678,45.51163.desc: An institution certified by the Canadian Council on Animal Care for its use of animals in science. Certificate of GAP Last visit: interim, April 2025. CCAC certification is a condition of federal research funding rather than a licence, so an institution outside it is not necessarily outside the work — it may simply not take federal money. The CCAC publishes names and certificate status and no addresses, so this point marks the institution rather than the building where animals are held.

27.63165,53.91643.name: Republican Research and Practical Center for Epidemiology and Microbiology (RPPCM)
27.63165,53.91643.desc: A BSL4 laboratory, operational. Run by Belarus Ministry of Health. It is categorised as a public health laboratory, working on human health. Personnel work in glove box. Containment space: 1589 SqM. Operational or announced: 2009. It stands in a built-up area, with more than fifty thousand people living within two and a half miles. There is no international register of laboratories at this containment level and no obligation to declare one, so this record comes from a research project rather than a regulator. What that project could not find out is absent here too.

-84.32550,33.79900.name: CDC ART clinic data
-84.32550,33.79900.desc: The clinic-by-clinic outcome data behind US fertility reporting: cycles, transfers, live births. It is the only place a prospective patient can compare clinics on results. The catch is structural — success rates depend heavily on which patients a clinic accepts, so a clinic can raise its published figures by declining harder cases, and the data cannot show you that.

105.77000,21.00000.name: Vietnam Academy of Agricultural Sciences
105.77000,21.00000.desc: Vietnam’s agricultural research system, in one of the largest rice-exporting countries in the world. Rice is where the food-security argument for engineering is strongest and where adoption has been slowest, because the export market has been the constraint rather than the science.

-106.67000,52.13300.name: Being sued over seed — Schmeiser and Bowman
-106.67000,52.13300.state: Saskatchewan — the Schmeiser farm, and the US Supreme Court
-106.67000,52.13300.desc: Two decisions define what a patent on a self-replicating organism means for the person growing it. In Canada, Monsanto v. Schmeiser held in 2004 that a farmer infringed by having the patented plant in his field, whatever the route by which it arrived, though he owed no damages having gained no benefit. In the United States, Bowman v. Monsanto held in 2013 that planting saved seed is making a new copy, not using a purchased one. Together they mean a grower can be liable for a plant they did not buy and did not want. It is the one place in this whole field where an ordinary person is the defendant, and worth knowing before it happens rather than after.
